situation.person: Thirty-year-old Lagos mother at 3 weeks postpartum in the first 12 weeks whose baby fusses after feeds, who pumps 20 millilitres and panics that the milk is gone
situation.specific_situation: She cannot tell whether the baby is full or starving, so she counts every wet nappy, weighs the baby on a kitchen scale, and scrolls signs of low supply at 3am without ever reaching certainty.
situation.timeframe: first 12 weeks whose baby fusses after
situation.trigger: Baby fussing after feeds with breasts that feel empty, plus relatives saying the milk is watery.
situation.problem: No trusted adequacy check exists, therefore anxiety decides every feed and unnecessary top-ups multiply.
situation.failed_attempt: Tried pap with tiger-nut and oats to bring milk, and nothing changed in two weeks except bloating; Googled and weighed him on a kitchen scale.
constraints: feels like her body failing him in front of the family
situation.emotional_stake: Breastfeeding equals her worth as a mother, so an empty-feeling breast feels like her body failing him in front of the family.
situation.desired_transformation: She can read wet nappies, weight gain and behaviour, and knows when a top-up is truly needed; the adequacy checklist is posted and followed.
